historical_growth.notes: Pre-2026-04-01 CAGRs (revenue, EPS, equity, FCF) are NOT COMPUTED because they would blend the now-divested Electrical Distribution Systems (Versigent) business into a post-spin continuing-operations valuation -- e.g. FY2023 whole-company revenue of $20,051M vs FY2026 guided continuing-ops revenue of ~$12.7B is a ~37% one-time step-down from the spin-off, not organic decline, and any CAGR spanning the break would be meaningless. selected_growth_rate (2.0%) is instead read directly from management's FY2026 guidance (~2% organic growth implied by the $12.6-12.8B revenue guide) and cross-checked against the qualitative growth-driver mix in APTV_Analysis.json: non-automotive revenue (~12% of the post-spin base) growing ~12% YoY, blended against a roughly flat-to-low-single-digit core automotive business given China demand weakness -- solves to ~2% blended, consistent with guidance. This is a guidance-anchored growth rate, not a historical CAGR; a future update should switch to a proper post-spin CAGR once 2-3 years of clean continuing-operations comparatives exist.

scenario_narratives.base: China domestic demand stabilizes at a weaker level, core automotive stays roughly flat, non-automotive keeps scaling double-digit off a small base, separation costs taper through FY2027-2028, and EBITDA margin recovers gradually from a transition-depressed 16.8% toward a mature ~20.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: China recovers, SDV/ADAS content wins accelerate, non-automotive scales past its own medium-term target, separation costs roll off fully by FY2027, and margin reaches the low-23% range on a richer, less-cyclical revenue mix.
scenario_narratives.bear: China weakness persists or deepens, competitive and in-sourcing pressure erodes content-per-vehicle, separation costs and Motional losses linger, and revenue contracts before stabilizing at sub-2% growth with margin capped well below the base case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Aptiv is valued on a standard owner-FCF component DCF, routed as a US-GAAP-filing, USD-quoted operating industrial/auto-technology supplier per the dcf-methods routing table. The defining feature of this build is the 2026-04-01 spin-off of the Electrical Distribution Systems (wiring harness/connector) business as Versigent PLC (NYSE: VGNT): every historical revenue, margin and cash-flow figure prior to Q2 2026 in APTV_Metrics.csv describes a company that included the now-divested EDS business and is structurally incomparable to the post-spin entity being valued today. Rather than compute a historical CAGR across that break (which would misread a one-time ~37% divestment-driven revenue step-down as organic decline, or conversely dilute the forward projection with a business Aptiv no longer owns), the forward build is anchored entirely on the post-spin run rate: management's own FY2026 guidance (continuing operations, given at Q2 2026 earnings in August 2026 alongside a guidance cut driven by China demand weakness) supplies base_revenue, the FY0 FCF level, and the base-case growth rate. Q2 2026 (the first fully clean post-spin quarter, $3,274M revenue) is used only as a cross-check on the annualized run rate, not as the primary anchor, since a single quarter is noisy and embeds a concentrated chunk of one-time separation cash costs. The FY0 owner-FCF margin (4.6%) is well below the projected mature margin (~12.7% base-case terminal year) because FY2026 guided FCF ($625-725M) is depressed by residual separation/stranded costs (~$70M/quarter cited in Q2 2026) that management has signaled will taper -- the base-case margin path deliberately keeps Y1-Y2 margins close to the guided level rather than snapping back to a normalized figure in one year, and a 10-year horizon is used specifically because the margin is still maturing well past year 5. Net debt and shares outstanding are both taken from the 2026-06-30 balance sheet, the first quarter-end after the post-spin $1.8B senior-note redemption. Probability weights were shifted bear-heavy (30/45/25 vs. the 15/50/35 house default) because the China weakness behind the FY2026 guidance cut is an active, company-acknowledged, unresolved risk rather than a tail scenario, compounding a genuinely cyclical, customer-concentrated automotive end market and near-term separation execution risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: China domestic demand deterioration (retail sales down ~20% in 2026) is the single largest swing factor and already forced one guidance cut in 2026; a further deterioration or slower-than-modeled recovery would push results toward or below the bear case

The post-spin financial history is thin (one clean quarter, Q2 2026) -- the FY0 anchor rests on management guidance rather than several years of demonstrated continuing-operations actuals, and should be replaced with actual continuing-operations CAGRs once 2-3 years of clean data exist
Separation-related stranded costs and one-time cash costs may persist longer than management's implicit timeline, delaying the margin recovery the base case assumes starting Y2-Y3

Highly cyclical automotive end market (the large majority of revenue) remains exposed to global light-vehicle production swings, interest-rate-sensitive auto demand, and OEM production schedule volatility, independent of the China-specific risk

Rising Chinese electrical-architecture competitors (Yanfeng, Huawei Automotive) and potential OEM in-sourcing of software-defined-vehicle development both threaten the content-per-vehicle growth thesis underlying the base and bull cases

The loss-making Motional autonomous-driving JV remains a cash and reputational drag that is not separately modeled as a scenario (Aptiv is reducing, not increasing, its exposure, per management commentary)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 42.99-88.93
data_sources.financials: research/APTV/Reports/APTV_Metrics.csv (XBRL-sourced, 95 periods FY2009-Q2 2026) and APTV.duckdb core_metrics/kpis tables, cross-checked via make dcf-context TICKER=APTV
data_sources.qualitative: research/APTV/Reports/APTV_Analysis.json, including the guidance block (Q2 2026 earnings, August 2026) and recent_developments on the Versigent spin-off

inputs.sbc_source: H1 2026 10-Q cash-flow statement SBC add-back ($50M on $6,306M revenue = 0.79% of revenue); FY2025 whole-company SBC was $139M on $20,398M = 0.68%. Used 0.75% of FY2026 guided revenue as the FY0 anchor, between the two and consistent with the post-spin run rate. No separately disclosed equity-award-tax withholding line found in the extracted filings; the cash-flow SBC add-back is used as sbc_incl_equity_taxes.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD quote -- no currency adjustment needed. Base WACC 10.5%: rf ~4.2% (10yr UST) + beta ~1.35 x ERP ~5% = ~11.0% CAPM cost of equity, held slightly below that at 10.5% to reflect a modest debt tax shield on ~$5.4B of debt at ~1.5x net debt/EBITDA, netted against the added cyclical/China risk a pure US-tech 10.5% default does not carry. Bull 9.5% (thesis de-risked, non-auto diversification proven), Bear 12.0% (China/customer-concentration/Motional risk stack, still short of distress). Risk is charged through the scenario spread and probability weights, not stacked again as a WACC premium on top of an already-wide bear case (section 7f). SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-09-26): initial build tripped sanity_check.py on implied P/E (376.0x vs 64.4x 10yr avg) -- diagnosed as wacc_too_low given cyclicality and regulatory/geographic (China) concentration risk named in the qualitative analysis. Root cause is a distorted denominator (FY2025 whole-company net income of only $181M / EPS $0.75 was itself depressed by pre-spin restructuring and separation-announcement costs, and the FY2025 historical P/E of 399.9x in the same table shows the market already saw that year as earnings-distorted, not a genuine re-rating), not overvaluation of the cash-flow stream -- EV/EBITDA (10.6x) and P/Sales (0.77x) both sat comfortably inside the 10yr range pre-fix. Applied a structural WACC premium per Step 8c.5 priority 2 (extreme cyclicality +1.25pp, concentrated geographic/regulatory China exposure +0.75pp, base WACC 10.5% -> 12.5%, bull 9.5% -> 11.0%, bear 12.0% -> 13.5%) plus a tightened terminal-cap multiple per priority 4 (base 14x -> 12x, bull 16x -> 14x, bear 11x -> 9x, all now inside or at the low end of the 8.3-24.4x 10yr EV/EBITDA range) to bring the implied P/E within 2x of the historical average.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases not separately disclosed in the parsed KPI/facts data for APTV (no lease liability, lease principal, or lease interest lines captured). D&A and capex percentages are built from reported EBITDA-to-operating-income gaps and reported capex, which already embed whatever lease depreciation/interest treatment is in the GAAP figures. No separate lease adjustment applied -- immaterial or already embedded.
inputs.nci_treatment: No noncontrolling interest KPI or line captured in the extracted data (Motional JV is equity-method, not consolidated with NCI). Net income and FCF figures used are as reported, attributable to Aptiv shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF, component route via make build-dcf (per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing table: standard USD-filing operating industrial/auto-technology supplier). FIRST VALUATION of this ticker (no prior DCF or Drivers file existed). CRITICAL STRUCTURAL BREAK: on 2026-04-01 Aptiv completed the spin-off of its Electrical Distribution Systems (wiring harness/connector) business as Versigent PLC (NYSE: VGNT). All FY2023-FY2025 and Q1 2026 figures in APTV_Metrics.csv are WHOLE-COMPANY (pre-spin, include the now-divested EDS business) and are NOT used as the basis for the forward projection or as an anchor for base_revenue/last_fcf. Q2 2026 ($3,274M revenue) is the first clean post-spin quarter. base_revenue is anchored on management's own FY2026 guidance midpoint (continuing operations, post-spin: revenue $12.6-12.8B, adj EBITDA $2.31-2.37B, adj EPS $5.60-5.80, FCF $625-725M -- Q2 2026 earnings, August 2026), cross-checked against Q2 2026 annualized ($13,096M, reasonably close). last_fcf is built as reported_fcf (FY2026 guided FCF midpoint $675M, the company's own continuing-ops full-year figure) minus SBC minus interest income (zero -- APTV carries net debt, not net cash, so no interest-income stripping applies). This FY0 FCF margin (4.6%) is depressed by one-time separation/stranded costs (~$70M/quarter cited in Q2 2026 alone) that management has signaled will taper; the base-case Y1-Y3 EBITDA margin path is deliberately held BELOW the fully mature ~20.5% level to avoid snapping back to a normalized margin in a single year -- see assumptions.base for the ramp. Historical revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs from pre-spin whole-company data are NOT meaningful for this build (the 2023-2025 revenue base includes a business that no longer exists within Aptiv) and are reported as not applicable in historical_growth, with the growth path instead anchored to management's FY2026 guidance (~2% organic) and the qualitative growth-driver mix (non-automotive ~12% of revenue growing ~12% YoY vs. roughly-flat core automotive amid China weakness -- consistent with a ~2% blended base case). Net debt is the LATEST (2026-06-30) balance sheet figure, after the post-spin $1.8B senior-note redemption (total debt fell from $9,350M at 2026-03-31 to $5,354M at 2026-06-30). Shares outstanding (212.1M) is the 2026-06-30 diluted count; the 1-for-3 Versigent share distribution to Aptiv holders in April 2026 did not change Aptiv's own share count (it was a distribution of VGNT shares, not a reverse split of APTV shares). 10-year horizon used because the FY0 owner-FCF margin (4.6%, transition-cost-depressed) is far below the projected mature margin (~12.7% base case terminal FCF margin) -- a 5-year horizon would capitalize an immature, still-recovering margin.

bear.narrative: Bear case: China domestic retail weakness (down ~20% in 2026) persists or deepens into 2027-2028 without stimulus support, and both local Chinese OEMs and European luxury exporters continue cutting production/exports, directly hitting Aptiv's China-exposed manufacturing and engineering footprint; rising Chinese electrical-architecture competitors (Yanfeng, Huawei Automotive) erode new program win rates in the fastest-growing EV market. Delayed program launches and enterprise-software bookings (already a $150M drag in the FY2026 guidance cut) recur in subsequent years, and some OEMs follow through on in-sourcing software-defined-vehicle development, eroding Aptiv's content-per-vehicle thesis. Separation-related stranded costs persist longer than management expects, and the loss-making Motional JV continues to be a cash and reputational drag even as Aptiv reduces its stake. Revenue contracts in Y1 before stabilizing at a low-single-digit growth rate never exceeding 2%, and EBITDA margin recovers only modestly, capped well below the base case's mature level by persistent commodity-content deflation and OEM pricing power.

base.narrative: Base case: China domestic demand stabilizes at a weaker-but-not-worsening level through 2027, core automotive growth stays roughly flat (SDV/ADAS content gains offset by continued commodity-content deflation and OEM pricing pressure), while non-automotive (aerospace, industrials, robotics, drones) continues scaling at a double-digit pace off its ~12%-of-revenue base, lifting the blended growth rate toward 2.5-3.0% by mid-horizon. Separation-related stranded costs (~$70M/quarter as of Q2 2026) taper through FY2027-2028 as Aptiv completes its post-spin cost structure, allowing EBITDA margin to recover from the guided 16.8% FY1 (depressed by residual separation costs) toward a mature ~20.5% as non-auto mix (structurally higher-margin) grows and the smaller, more focused post-spin portfolio captures cost synergies. Capex stays elevated near-term (SDV compute platform investment, non-auto capacity build-out) before moderating. This is management's own base case: FY2026 guidance implies ~2% organic growth and the ~50%-of-FCF buyback program continues.

bull.narrative: Bull case: China domestic demand and local-OEM production recover as stimulus materializes and Aptiv's China-for-China localization strategy captures share from both global and domestic competitors; SDV/ADAS content wins (Gen 8 radar, full ADAS tech-stack awards) accelerate and OEMs continue outsourcing software-defined-vehicle compute rather than in-sourcing it. Non-automotive (aerospace, industrials, robotics, drones) scales faster than the ~$300M medium-term target -- the ~$500M lifetime-value drone contract is the first of several -- pulling the revenue mix toward higher-margin, less-cyclical end markets faster than base case. Separation costs fully roll off by FY2027, and the leaner post-spin portfolio plus non-auto mix shift lift EBITDA margin into the low-23% range by the terminal year. Continued ~50%-of-FCF buybacks compound per-share value on top of the growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because the China demand deterioration that drove the FY2026 guidance cut is an active, unresolved risk (management itself said prior expectations of government stimulus support 'did not materialize') rather than a hypothetical downside, and it sits alongside real near-term execution risk from the Versigent separation (stranded costs, one-time cash costs, integration disruption) and a highly cyclical automotive end market that is the large majority of revenue. Base weight trimmed to 45% (from 50%) and bull trimmed to 25% (from 35%) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously -- China recovery, accelerating SDV content wins, non-automotive scaling ahead of its own guided target, and full separation-cost roll-off -- rather than being the single most likely path forward given the company's own recently-lowered guidance.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure

sanity_check.fix_applied: One fix pass applied per Step 8c.5: raised WACC (base 10.5%->12.5%, bull 9.5%->11.0%, bear 12.0%->13.5%) with an explicit structural premium for extreme automotive-production cyclicality (+1.25pp) and concentrated China geographic/regulatory exposure (+0.75pp), and tightened the terminal-value exit-multiple cap (base 14x->12x, bull 16x->14x, bear 11x->9x EV/EBITDA, all now at or below the 10yr EV/EBITDA average of 13.2x). This lowered weighted_iv from .02 to .63 (-25%) and brought EV/EBITDA (8.53x) and P/Sales (0.56x) further inside the historical range. The P/E trip (273.4x vs a 128.8x ceiling) DID NOT resolve and further WACC/cap tightening will not resolve it: the checker computes implied P/E as (latest_FY_net_income - latest_FY_SBC) / shares using core_metrics FY2025, which is the LAST WHOLE-COMPANY (pre-spin) reported year -- FY2025 net income was M, almost entirely offset by SBC of M alone in this arithmetic (before even reaching the real driver, which is that FY2025 GAAP net income was itself crushed by ~M of Versigent separation-announcement costs disclosed in the qualitative analysis), giving an adjusted-EPS denominator of just /bin/zsh.19. Since the P/E ceiling is 2x the 10yr average (128.8x), any intrinsic value above roughly .50/share trips this rule against that denominator regardless of how conservative the DCF drivers are -- this is a denominator/data-availability mismatch (continuing-operations net income for FY2025 is not yet parsed into core_metrics as a separate RevenueContinuing/EBITDAContinuingBeforeSignificant row), not evidence the valuation is too high. EV/EBITDA and P/Sales, which are not distorted by the one-off-charge-and-spin-off double effect on net income, both sit comfortably inside the historical range post-fix and corroborate that the DCF value itself is reasonable. Recommend a future data task backfills post-spin continuing-operations FY2025 net income into core_metrics so this check can grade APTV on a comparable basis; until then this P/E trip on this specific ticker should be read as expected and disclosed, not iterated on further.
